newsitem.title: USA: US transport dept backs San Francisco BART project.
newsitem.headline: US transport dept backs San Francisco BART project.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Transportation has affirmed its support for the $1.2 billion Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) District extension project, the district said on Thursday.

In a letter to members of Congress, the Federal Transit Administration and the Federal Aviation Administration approved of BART's financial plan for building the extension to the San Francisco International Airport, BART said.
The letter affirmed that the cost-sharing agreement between BART and the airport, which will contribute up to $200 million to the project, adheres to federal rules, BART said.
Critics claimed that funding from the San Francisco Airport for the BART extension project would constitute an illegal revenue diversion.

BART General Manager Thomas Margro said he hoped the letter would pave the way for federal officials to quickly issue a full funding grant agreement, which will set out a federal commitment of $750 million for the project. Funding for the project will also include $200 million from the airport, $108 million from the state, and about $110 million from other sources.
Depending on the timing of the full funding grant agreement, BART said it could break ground on the project next month.
